comments.text:
I'd argue that resistance training wins by a far wider margin considering skeletal muscle also burns more calories daily forever in to the future. Just as an example if someone is 90kg at 30% body fat they have 27kg of fat. Their TDEE at 0 gym exercise is somewhere around 2075.

If they used the nothing but diet and lose 10kg in the 70/30 rate from the study they lose 7kg of fat and 3 kg of other tissue and are now 80kg with 20kg of fat. That makes them now 25% fat. Their TDEE is now basically 2000. They lost 225 calories or one donut every 3 days.

If instead they did the resistance training they lose 12kg of fat but gain 2kg of skeletal muscle they are 80kg with 15kg of fat or 18.75% which puts their TDEE at 0 gym activity at about 2130.

That means they gained 55 calories a day or a donut every 5 days for "free" just from their daily movement.

So not only did they lose more fat, got to a really great body fat percentage, but also expanded their calories requirements so maintaining their weight just got easier. It's like a win-win-win plus donut win.

comments.text: I think this study is great, as it reinforces why resistance training is so important for high-quality weight loss, which targets fat loss while preserving lean mass. However, the cardio in this study was at ~65% of MHR while RT began at moderate effort and participants progressed to work harder throughout. So the stimulus applied between the RT and aerobic groups were different. I just want to point out that while weight lifting is without a doubt the better method to gain muscle mass, cardio that works against a resistance at similar effort levels (hills, intervals, torque work, etc) would substantially increase fat loss rate and can also help to preserve or make muscle gains. I get way leaner when mountain bike season rolls around even though I lift all year round. Same with running. And I'm not a beginner, but response is still at a solid rate. There are also numerous studies to show this. And I agree, combining both weights and cardio is the optimal method along with a sensible deficit.
